evidence: Swap test fails: a seed library, toy library or allotment-plot booking could take the find/basket/confirm frame unchanged (white bordered cards on pale grey-green, one dark-green filled button, bold sans headings, a single green wrench mark beside the name in body-weight text). Only the copy (sessions, deposits, volunteers, 14 Mill Lane) is bound to this product.

Category-guess test fails: predicted default for a council/community booking flow is a GOV.UK-style frame: white ground, one sans, one green or blue primary, bordered cards, error summary box with red rule, radio cards. All of these are present (find 1280-light, basket errors 375-light, confirm 1280-light).

Similar-prompt test fails: a brief for 'a library-of-things reservation for a repair cafe' would land on the same card grid with an identical icon thumbnail per item, the same summary list on confirm and the same 'What happens next' box on done.

Product-bound elements that survive: the pick-up day calendar that marks library sessions as 'Open' (tool day-chosen 1280-light, dot variant at 375) and the copy voice ('Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence', 'We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower'). These are content and mechanism, not an identity layer.

unfinished: ten identical wrench-icon placeholder thumbnails on pale green squares in place of tool images (find 1280-light, 375-light)
identity is only the name set in bold body-size text with a small wrench glyph in the masthead; no designed mark
headings differ from body only by size and weight; no typographic moment on any page
no focal point on find: a uniform 2x5 grid of equal cards
flat empty band of page ground below the footer on basket, done and confirm at 1280 (footer stops short)
sticky 'Reserve this tool' bar cuts across the calendar so a row of days is hidden (tool day-chosen 1280-light, default 375-light)
stranded 'Oct' on its own line inside availability badges at 375; tool names truncated with ellipsis so the two cordless drills read the same
basket session cards: one full-width card then five squeezed cards with three-line wraps, in reverse date order (basket 1280-light)
evidence: First viewport of find at 1280: heading 'Find a tool', a paragraph, a full-width search field, then the start of an even grid of identical cards; nothing on the page rewards a look beyond the information.
After a scroll: the same card repeated ten times, then 'Opening times' as a heading and a paragraph, then a one-line footer.
Done page: a definition list in a box and a 'What happens next' box, with a large empty band under the footer at 1280.
Clean and orderly, coherent token use and readable copy, but it reads as a default service form; I would not expect the owner to be proud of how it looks, only that it works.
